thread:
Sasha: Heads up — seeing a spike of kubelet NetCheck failures on gpu nodes in us-west-2. Several long-running trainer pods got deleted by the node-level probe. Anyone else?
Priya: saw 5 alerts in the last 10m, all on nodes in asg-gpu-usw2a.
infra-alerts-bot: [ALERT] netcheck_failure on node gpu-014 — 2026-03-18T14:05:10Z
Marco: quick check — are these the new AMIs rolled last night?
Sasha: yes, 014/015/016 were part of the kernel-sched rollout. We thought net changes were minimal.
Li: logs from kubelet say: ```Mar 18 14:03:09 kubelet[1]: network health probe failed: read udp 10.0.2.1:42222->10.0.2.2:8472: packet too big
kernel: eth0: warning: mtu mismatch: if_mtu 1500 != hw_mtu 9000
```
Priya: mtu mismatch + packet too big — we have mixed MTU config (9000 on host NIC, 1500 in CNI). That explains UDP probes failing.
Marco: that would trigger the netcheck probe to mark node NotReady and evict pods if probe threshold hit, right? :grimacing:
Sasha: yes kubelet's net-probe uses UDP pings to kube-proxy iptables svc IP, failed probes => considered node-unhealthy.
Li: consequence: autoscaler sees pods fail and tries to reschedule, causing GPU churn and capacity spikes. A few paid training runs restarted.
Priya: quick mitigation: bump kubelet flag `--node-status-update-frequency`? or increase net-probe timeout/threshold? We can also disable net-probe temporarily.
Marco: ops suggestion: add a canary tweak to kubelet config on one ASG to increase `--network-plugin-timeout=20s` and `--register-node=false`? Not sure about register-node.
Sasha: short-term I can flip the CNI MTU to 9000 on those hosts (we control kernel) or revert AMI. Which is less blasty?
Li: reverting AMI is safer but slower. Changing CNI is quick but risk of inconsistency across AZs. If we change CNI, we must roll the CNI daemonset and restart kube-proxy.
infra-alerts-bot: [INFO] Started automated rollback ticket: #INF-4821
Priya: I'd prefer disable net-probe on the affected nodes for 30m: `kubectl annotate node gpu-014 debug.kubelet.netcheck=disabled` — kubelet respects certain debug toggles? (not by default)
Marco: alternative: patch `kubelet-config` configmap for the ASG with relaxed net thresholds and rollout via MachineDeployments. Low risk if we target only gpu ASG.
Sasha: plan: 1) Pause AMI rollout (ops). 2) Patch CNI MTU loop on gpu ASG to 9000 and restart cni pods (quick test on gpu-014). 3) If not fixed in 20m, revert AMI. I'll own the test and report back.
Li: if we need to avoid immediate evictions, we can add `tolerations` on training pods to survive node NotReady for a short grace — but that masks real network issues.
Priya: noted cost implication: restarted jobs consumed ~3 GPU-hours across two customers. Logging incident for chargeback.
Sasha: starting with a canary now on gpu-014. Pinging @Marco to help with cni ds rollout.
Marco: on it. pushing a patch to reconcile MTU in cni config: `{"name":"mtu","value":9000}` and rolling ds on nodes with label gpu=true.
kubelet-bot: [action] NetCheck probe suppressed on node gpu-014 by admin command at 14:12Z
Sasha: canary looks good so far, probes recovered after cni restart on gpu-014 — node back to Ready and pods stable. Monitoring the rest of the pool.
Priya: thanks. Let's queue an infra postmortem tomorrow: root cause = AMI kernel/host MTU vs CNI MTU mismatch causing false-positive netcheck evictions on GPU nodes.
Sasha: adding runbook entry: before kernel upgrades, verify host MTU vs CNI settings, and add a canary gate for gpu ASGs.
Marco: will also add a Grafana panel for NetCheck failure rate per ASG + correlate with kernel deployment tags.
Sasha: closing thread; watch alerts for 30m and update #INF-4821 with timelines.
Li: thanks all :thumbsup:
